list.ambiguousTitle: A role name is carried by more than one role node
list.ambiguousNames: An access control entry holds a role name, and Jahia resolves it with a query that takes the first result. So which permissions apply is undefined for these names: {{names}}
list.missingDeclared: {{count}} role the installed sources declare is not in this repository. Restoring it puts the role back, and the access control entries that named it start granting again.
list.missingDeclared_plural: {{count}} roles the installed sources declare are not in this repository. Restoring one puts the role back, and the access control entries that named it start granting again.

confirm.deleteHeld: {{count}} access control entry grants this role, to {{principals}}. That entry stays behind naming a role that no longer exists, and it then grants nothing.
confirm.deleteUnused: No access control entry grants this role, so nobody loses access.
confirm.deleteSubRoles: The roles nested inside it go with it: {{names}}.
confirm.deletePermissions: It names {{count}} permission of its own.
confirm.removeTargetMessage: The role stops granting anything on {{path}}, and this cannot be undone.
confirm.removeTargetPermissions: The permission this target names goes with it: {{names}}.
confirm.deleteHeld_plural: {{count}} access control entries grant this role, to {{principals}}. Those entries stay behind naming a role that no longer exists, and they then grant nothing.
confirm.deletePermissions_plural: It names {{count}} permissions of its own.
confirm.removeTargetPermissions_plural: The {{count}} permissions this target names go with it: {{names}}.

dialog.blocked: The {{role}} role grants {{permission}}, so no change here removes it. Open that role instead.
dialog.cascades: Removing {{permission}} also removes the {{count}} permissions it grants.
dialog.expands: {{ancestor}} is granted, and it grants {{permission}}. Removing it replaces that one grant with {{count}} explicit grants.
dialog.collapse: {{count}} grants are replaced by one grant on {{permission}}.
dialog.blockedButNamed: This role names {{permission}}, and the {{role}} role grants it too. Removing the name here leaves the permission granted by {{role}}.

reset.title: Reset the {{role}} role
reset.baseline: This restores what the installed sources declare for this role: {{sources}}. That is what a new instance running this Jahia version with these modules would hold, and not the state the role had before it was edited.
reset.incomplete: The baseline is incomplete: {{sources}} could not be read. The reset could remove a permission one of those sources in fact declares.
reset.recreates: The repository no longer has this role, so the reset creates it. The access control entries left behind by its deletion name it again, and the access they carried returns.
reset.addsReach: The role then grants {{count}} permission here.
reset.removesReach: The role stops granting {{count}} permission here.
reset.keptTarget: {{path}} is left alone. No source declares it, so the baseline carries nothing to restore there.
reset.typeToConfirm: The role would grant more than it does today. Type this to confirm
reset.notDeclared: No installed source declares this role, so there is no baseline to reset to. A role your team created has none, and neither does a role generated per language.
reset.alreadyMatches: This role already matches what the sources declare, so a reset would write nothing.
reset.planFailed: The baseline could not be read.
reset.stale: The role changed while this was open. Close the dialog and read the difference again.
reset.addsReach_plural: The role then grants {{count}} permissions here, because an added name grants its {{extra}} descendants too.
reset.removesReach_plural: The role stops granting {{count}} permissions here, because a removed name granted its {{extra}} descendants too.
reset.roleGroupCleared: the scope is removed, because no source declares one
reset.textChange: the title and the description in {{languages}}
reset.textChange_plural: the title and the description in {{languages}}
